newsitem.title: USA: Emaciated U.S. twins upgraded to serious condition.
newsitem.headline: Emaciated U.S. twins upgraded to serious condition.

text.p: Five-year-old twin girls who were found emaciated, crawling with ants and encrusted with excrement in their California home were in slightly better condition Wednesday, a hospital spokeswoman said.
The twins, being treated at Oakland Children's Hospital, were upgraded from critical to serious, spokeswoman Jeanette Rogers said.

The twins' mother, 26-year-old Tanya Walker, appeared in court in California's central valley town of Modesto Tuesday to be arraigned on charges of attempted murder, torture and child endangerment. She could face a life prison sentence if convicted, police say.
In a trembling voice, Walker, dressed in orange prison uniform, denied the charges against her and told the judge she wanted to go home to see her family.

Twins Brittany and Breanne, who suffer from cerebral palsy, were severely malnourished, dehydrated and bruised when they were found in bunkbeds in a house in Ceres, 80 miles (130 kms) east of San Francisco, on Sunday night, police said.
A police statement said the girls were "suffering from scabies, had dried stool particles around their buttocks and had ants crawling in and out of bodily orifices."
Ceres Police Sgt. Allen McKay said the twins, who weighed just 14 and 19 pounds, looked like Holocaust victims and "were just basically skin and bones."
Walker was arrested on Sunday night and jailed.
Neighbours and social workers, who visited the home in April, said they had no idea of the situation.

The girls' grandparents found the twins alone, locked inside Walker's home on Sunday when they were returning two siblings from a weekend visit. The grandparents took the twins to a nearby hospital and police were notified. The twins were later flown to Oakland Children's Hospital.

At the time the children were found, Walker had gone to pick up her infant son from a babysitter. Walker also has two other healthy children, the 3-year-old son and 7-year-old daughter who had been visiting the grandparents. The three other children were released to relatives, police said.

Walker told police that government funding was cut off for a nutritional formula that had been prescribed for the twins. She tried other foods but the twins lost weight and their condition deteriorated to a point where she was afraid to seek medical help because she was concerned authorities would take her other children away from her, McKay said.
